entities.name: PMID:10755569
observations: Sonoda et al. studied orthotopic murine corneal transplantation in ICAM-1−/− versus wild-type C57BL/6 recipients using BALB/c, BALB.b, and B10.D2 donor corneas.
For B10.D2 grafts, long-term acceptance was 100% in ICAM-1−/− recipients versus 58% in wild-type recipients (P=0.006), and no ICAM-1−/− recipients developed donor-specific DTH.
No survival difference was observed for fully mismatched BALB/c or minor-antigen-mismatched BALB.b grafts; the effect was mismatch-dependent.
Evidence is from a single primary mouse study, with the retrieved record limited to abstract-level detail and no independent replication identified.

entities.name: ICAM1
observations: ICAM-1 deficiency suppressed donor-specific alloantigen DTH and improved long-term acceptance in the tested B10.D2 MHC-disparate corneal transplant model, but did not improve survival for BALB/c or BALB.b grafts.

entities.name: Corneal allograft rejection
observations: ICAM-1 deficiency reduced rejection in the B10.D2 MHC-disparate mouse corneal transplant model, but not across the BALB/c or BALB.b disparity models.
